title: Introduction to simulacr
text: simulacr implements outbreak simulation using contact-driven branching processes. main features package include: simulate_outbreak(): main function, simulating epidemic spread using inputs generation time distribution, individual transmission rates, contact matrices; outputs simulacr object, list containing linelist transmission tree, can converted epicontacts igraph objects, plotted using plot() simulate_outbreak_step(): step-wise version simulator, designed calling packages make_pmf_delay(): generate probability mass functions delays distributions make_disc_gamma(): build discretised Gamma distributions delay distributions make_panmictic_contacts(): generate contact matrix assuming random mixing draw_labels(): wrapper function generate random alphanumeric labels

title: Introduction to simulacr
text: brief example illustrates can simulate outbreak.  save animation GIF, use optional gifski package.
code: ## make a generation time distribution gen_time <- make_pmf_delay(make_disc_gamma(10, 7)) plot(   gen_time(0:30),   type = "h",   lend = 2,   lwd = 10,   main = "Generation time distribution",   xlab = "Delay from primary to secondary infection (days)",   ylab = "p(delay)" ) ## simulate an outbreak using random mixing ## (no contacts matrix provided -> all individuals are in contact by default) set.seed(1) res <- simulate_outbreak(   n = 100, # 100 individuals in the population   duration = 365, # simulate for a year   w = gen_time, # generation time distribution   tau = runif(100, 0.01, 0.05) # individual transmission rates, from 0.01 to 0.05 )  names(res) #> [1] "linelist" "tree" res #> $linelist #> # A tibble: 100 × 3 #>    id     casedef date_infection #>    <chr>  <chr>            <dbl> #>  1 eLGzdD case                 1 #>  2 8Tvbyj case                40 #>  3 MQ90i6 case                33 #>  4 RdzUUA case                25 #>  5 kSVCEa case                45 #>  6 Z42dvb case                32 #>  7 YWzVgb case                44 #>  8 EGjSAk case                31 #>  9 6rcYKS case                52 #> 10 VBW4HD case                51 #> # ℹ 90 more rows #>  #> $tree #> # A tibble: 96 × 3 #>    from   to      date #>    <chr>  <chr>  <dbl> #>  1 NA     eLGzdD     1 #>  2 eLGzdD LjuhEd    13 #>  3 LjuhEd HmhA3k    17 #>  4 LjuhEd J98DE8    22 #>  5 HmhA3k Lwe2aP    22 #>  6 LjuhEd MOZ5Ca    22 #>  7 MOZ5Ca yKVg67    24 #>  8 HmhA3k knhTUJ    24 #>  9 J98DE8 3eZzb4    24 #> 10 Lwe2aP RdzUUA    25 #> # ℹ 86 more rows #>  #> attr(,"class") #> [1] "simulacr" "list" plot(res) gifski::save_gif(   animate_outbreak(res, t = 1:max(res$tree$date)),   gif_file = "outbreak.gif",   delay = 0.2 )

title: Create a contact matrix according to individual contact rates — make_random_contacts
code: ## 4 individuals, no contact with rate = 0 res <- make_random_contacts(4, 0) res #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] #> [1,]    0    0    0    0 #> [2,]    0    0    0    0 #> [3,]    0    0    0    0 #> [4,]    0    0    0    0  ## same with higher rate res <- make_random_contacts(4, 2.5) res #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] #> [1,]    0    1    0    1 #> [2,]    0    0    0    1 #> [3,]    1    1    0    0 #> [4,]    0    2    0    0  ## 6 individuals with some Poisson-distributed heterogeneity in rates, ## average 5.6 contacts per day, except for indiv 2 (rate 500) and 3  ## (rate (0))  rates <- rpois(6, 5.6) rates[2] <- 500 rates[3] <- 0 set.seed(1) # only to compare results with next example res <- make_random_contacts(6, rates) res #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6] #> [1,]    0    0    1    3    0    0 #> [2,]  103    0   93   87  101  108 #> [3,]    0    0    0    0    0    0 #> [4,]    1    0    0    0    0    0 #> [5,]    4    1    1    1    0    3 #> [6,]    3    0    1    2    3    0  ## same, binary output (fixing seed for comparable results) res_nb <- res set.seed(1) res <- make_random_contacts(6, rates, TRUE) res_nb #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6] #> [1,]    0    0    1    3    0    0 #> [2,]  103    0   93   87  101  108 #> [3,]    0    0    0    0    0    0 #> [4,]    1    0    0    0    0    0 #> [5,]    4    1    1    1    0    3 #> [6,]    3    0    1    2    3    0 res  #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6] #> [1,]    0    0    1    1    0    0 #> [2,]    1    0    1    1    1    1 #> [3,]    0    0    0    0    0    0 #> [4,]    1    0    0    0    0    0 #> [5,]    1    1    1    1    0    1 #> [6,]    1    0    1    1    1    0

what: Simulate outbreaks with transmission trees — simulate_outbreak
title: Simulate outbreaks with transmission trees — simulate_outbreak
text: function implements contact-driven branching process outbreak simulator. Outbreaks start single infection otherwise fully susceptible population size non first time step. New cases generated time step infectious individuals, forces infection depending generation time distribution, individual transmission rates, contacts individuals. function returns linelist including non-cases cases, well transmission tree listing transmission events shape data.frame columns , , date. function user-facing; use simulacr engine another package, may want use low-level function [simulate_outbreak_step()].

title: Simulate outbreaks with transmission trees — simulate_outbreak
code: simulate_outbreak(   n,   duration = 1L,   w = c(0, 1),   tau = 0,   contacts = NULL,   label_size = 6 )

title: Simulate outbreaks with transmission trees — simulate_outbreak
text: n integer indicating number individuals population; default. duration integer indicating number time steps run simulation ; defaults 1L (.e. initial infection generated). w probability mass function generation time distribution, produced [make_pmf_delay()], specified numeric vector, function, distcrete object. Defaults point mass 1 (.e. secondary infections take place exactly 1 time step primary infection). tau numeric vector length n containing individual transmission rates; single value recycled; defaults 0 (transmission). contacts Contacts individuals population. can specified two ways: ) n x n matrix entries correspond contact presence intensities, ii) function single argument t (time step) generating matrix time step. NULL (default), assume random-mixing population, .e. individuals contact every time step. label_size integer indicating length labels generated [draw_labels()], used unique individual identifiers. Defaults 6.

title: Simulate outbreaks with transmission trees — simulate_outbreak
text: force infection (FOI) individual \(\) \(j\) time \(t\) defined : \(\lambda_{t, \rightarrow j} = I_{t,} C_{t, \rightarrow j} \tau_{t,} w(t - T_i)\) total FOI experienced individual  time  summed possible sources infection: \(\lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j} = S_{t,j} \sum_i \lambda_{t, \rightarrow j} \) follows individual \(j\) becomes infected time \(t+1\) according Bernoulli distribution probability: \( 1 - e^{-\lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j}} \) keep track chains transmission, infector \(j\), denoted \(alpha_j\), drawn Multinomial distribution weighted respective FOIs directed towards \(j\): \( \alpha_j \sim \mathcal{M}(1, \lambda_{t, 1 \rightarrow j} / \lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j} ,\lambda_{t, 2 \rightarrow j} / \lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j} , \ldots , \lambda_{t, N \rightarrow j} / \lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j}  ) \)
